webpage_capture_policy: For a readable webpage, the default development path is interactive read -> faithful claim-scoped visible-text capture plus source/provenance metadata -> bounded local database capture capsule -> Google Drive handoff. Do not invoke GitHub Actions merely to fetch or archive webpage HTML. The local database is a capture/handoff envelope, not live PostgreSQL authority and not automatic Fact/Judgment publication. Preserve original URL, publisher/source identity, title/date when supported, capture timestamp, capture_mode, visible text, text SHA-256 and any material limitation.
github_release_policy: During development, PDFs that require raw source-byte preservation use the existing GitHub Actions acquisition lane: fetch the public PDF, validate/hash it, package it under a unique immutable name, publish it to GitHub Release, then verify the published bytes. Do not use Actions/Release as the default path for readable webpages or HTML merely to preserve page text. A runner retrieval failure for one host is not permission to call the source unavailable or to discard other successfully acquired PDF bytes.
google_drive_policy: Google Drive is the development handoff relay for bounded local webpage-capture databases and Longcycle-generated binary state: DuckDB/SQLite webpage capture capsules, replay materializations, execution/reconciliation outputs, generated database snapshots and offline runtimes. A webpage capture capsule contains source-derived visible text and provenance, so Drive transport does not turn that text into a generated research conclusion or change source authority. Do not put raw PDF source bytes in Drive by default; PDFs use the Actions -> Release lane. Drive is not live transactional database authority.
postgres_policy: Do not transport a live PostgreSQL cluster as session state or place it in GitHub Release. PostgreSQL remains the transactional write/ops engine and is rebuilt in a service-capable runtime when writes, leases or outbox semantics are required. If a generated database snapshot is ever needed for handoff, it belongs in Google Drive and remains a snapshot rather than live authority.
duckdb_policy: DuckDB is the preferred bounded local container for webpage visible-text capture capsules and portable read/replay state; SQLite is an acceptable bounded capture envelope when DuckDB is not available in the current interactive runtime. Before handoff, checkpoint/close the capsule, record SHA-256/size/schema/source count, upload the immutable capsule to Google Drive, and verify the downloaded bytes. After restore, research/replay capsules open read-only by default. Raw PDF source bytes required for re-grounding are restored separately from GitHub Release.
legacy_release_web_policy: Previously produced immutable Release assets that include webpage/HTML bytes are grandfathered. Never mutate or silently relocate them. All new readable webpage captures follow local database -> Google Drive unless a future explicit architecture decision supersedes this policy.
historical_asset_index_policy: This manifest is resume-relevant, not an exhaustive historical asset inventory. Assets no longer required by the live continuation cursor may be pruned from this file without deleting or invalidating them; durable research/execution receipts plus Git history retain their exact Release/Drive identities and restore hashes. Re-enter an old workstream through its durable receipt rather than keeping every historical binary in fresh-Agent context.
supersession_policy: All handoff transports are immutable-by-identity. Never replace bytes behind a recorded Release filename or Drive file id without advancing the repository manifest and SHA-256. Successor PDF source packs get new Release filenames; successor webpage-capture/generated packs get new Drive files/ids.

assets.content_summary: Two runner-stable original PDF sources for the bounded SV-005 first replay: the FDA/Federal Register legal revocation notice and GSK's DREAMM-7 stock-exchange announcement. The pack was built deterministically, uploaded under a unique name and downloaded back with outer-SHA verification. The accessdata.fda.gov historical label/approval-package endpoints were deliberately excluded after three fail-closed runner diagnostics; the 2020 FDA approval/safety source is preserved separately through the readable-webpage capsule.
